selected.name: Identification of Hidden Flaws in Paradigms
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the abstract explicitly diagnoses a subtle, previously unrecognized flaw, mathematical instability, or conceptual bottleneck in widely used standard methods. Score 0 if it simply builds on top of standard paradigms without questioning their foundations.
selected.rationale: Dense-favored abstracts (R18, R34) identify hidden flaws in standard setups (e.g., standard concentration ignoring label uncertainty, edge-of-stability dynamics). Scorecard-favored ones (R07, R19) do not diagnose underlying flaws. The dense model rewards foundational critique.
member_names: Identification of Hidden Flaws in Paradigms
Information density relative to abstract length
Result contradicts a stated prevailing belief

selected.name: Unifying Abstraction Across Regimes
selected.instruction: Score 10 when one clearly defined principle explains or operates across genuinely different settings, with the mapping between settings made explicit; score 0 when multiple applications are merely listed without a shared abstraction.
selected.rationale: R18 uses frame averaging for several symmetry families while preserving a common formal guarantee. R46 transfers neural rendering ideas from vision into wireless propagation through an explicit path-based analogy.

selected.name: Confound Isolation
selected.instruction: Score 10 when comparisons, controls or ablations separate competing explanations for the observed effect; score 0 when several factors change together and the claimed cause cannot be isolated from the abstract.
selected.rationale: R21 separates clean and adversarial normalization statistics, R25 decomposes weight balancing into distinct mechanisms, and R30 tests whether interference depends on semantic relatedness. These controls support causal interpretation rather than association.

selected.name: Resolution of Fundamental Trade-offs
selected.instruction: 10 = Abstract demonstrates a method that breaks a well-known trade-off (e.g., efficiency vs. accuracy) through a novel insight (e.g., R03, R27); 0 = Abstract merely shifts a trade-off slightly along the Pareto frontier using more data or compute (e.g., R13, R34).
selected.rationale: Overcoming classical limits is a hallmark of exceptional research that the scorecard fails to recognize if standard metrics aren't heavily featured.

selected.name: Failure-Mechanism Fit
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract identifies a concrete failure mechanism and the proposed design directly addresses that mechanism; score 0 when it states a generic problem and adds an unmotivated technique.
selected.rationale: R04 diagnoses noisy addressing, aliasing, and linkage degradation before matching each to a specific fix. R14 identifies recall and comparison deficits in SSMs and designs H3 around those capabilities.

selected.name: Domain-Valid Inductive Bias
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the representation or architecture encodes a domain symmetry, geometry, interaction law or physical constraint and explains why that structure is appropriate; score 0 when the architecture is domain-agnostic without justification.
selected.rationale: R27 builds exact symmetry into frame averaging, R52 represents directional long-range interactions, and R45 generates molecules from realistic structural motifs. These domain-aligned choices are strong quality signals beyond generic architectural novelty.
member_names: Novel Inductive Bias over Pure Scaling

selected.name: Theory–Algorithm Closure
selected.instruction: Score 10 when formal assumptions, guarantees or complexity bounds directly characterize the proposed algorithm and its use; score 0 when theory is absent or disconnected from the practical method.
selected.rationale: R07 connects misaligned-gradient assumptions to explicit iteration complexities, while R46 turns an information-theoretic limit into an executable estimator. This tight closure is underrepresented in more benchmark-oriented abstracts such as R04.

selected.name: Mechanistic explanation of why, not just what
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the abstract explains the underlying causal mechanism or reason WHY an observed phenomenon or result occurs, rather than merely stating what was done and what improved. A 10: the abstract states a specific causal hypothesis or mechanism (e.g., a distributional mismatch, an uncertainty gap) and explains how it produces the observed effect. A 0: the abstract lists a technique and a resulting number/improvement with no explanation of why it works.
selected.rationale: R01 builds and tests a 'two-domain hypothesis' to explain why batch normalization hurts adversarial robustness, and R48 introduces label uncertainty specifically to explain why concentration-of-measure fails to capture intrinsic robustness -- both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R33 (dense_low_card_high) states two engineering fixes mapped to two observed problems but does not develop a deeper causal account.
member_names: Explains why, not only reports that
Mechanistic explanation of why, not just what

selected.name: Contribution by subtraction or simplification
selected.instruction: Score whether the work advances by removing, fixing, or simplifying machinery while preserving capability, as opposed to adding stages. 10 = the paper shows a widely used component is unnecessary, replaces a complex procedure with a markedly simpler or cheaper one, or reduces a multi-stage pipeline to fewer stages, and is explicit that the simpler version matches or nearly matches what it replaces. 5 = a method of ordinary complexity with a genuine efficiency argument. 0 = the contribution is strictly additive -- new modules, extra training phases, extra preference categories, extra generation steps -- with no accounting of what could have been dropped.
selected.rationale: R26 (the last weight layer can be fixed entirely, with memory and speed benefits), R59 (transforming a diffusion model back into a classical denoising autoencoder), and R27 (easier to implement, faster to compute, five times shorter training) all take value away from the system and still deliver. Rubric banks reward described machinery, so additive designs such as R13 (five preference aspects plus a new optimization objective) and R16 (motif vocabulary, focal selection, attachment, cheminformatics, refinement) accumulate credit for each added part, while subtractive papers present less surface to score.

selected.name: Cross-domain conceptual transfer
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract explicitly imports a concept or technique from a distant field/application area into a new one, naming the source analogy. A 10: the abstract explicitly draws an analogy to a different domain's method and adapts it. A 0: the work stays entirely within its home domain's standard toolkit with no cross-domain framing.
selected.rationale: R06 explicitly transplants the NeRF idea from vision into wireless channel modeling, and R21 explicitly extends the 2D Segment-Anything idea into the 3D point-cloud domain -- both dense_high_card_low. R33's object-detection distillation stays within the established knowledge-distillation toolkit with no such transfer -- dense_low_card_high.

selected.name: Exact Mathematical Guarantees over Heuristics
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the method explicitly provides mathematically exact properties (e.g., 'exact invariance,' 'provably optimal,' 'guaranteed bounds'). Score 0 if the method relies entirely on heuristic approximations, empirical validations, and probabilistic guesses.
selected.rationale: Dense-favored abstracts (R02, R21) highlight exact guarantees (near-optimal performance, exact equivariance). Scorecard-favored ones (R51, R16) rely on heuristic adjustments. The dense model strongly prefers provable exactness over heuristic tuning.

selected.name: Resource Accounting for Practicality
selected.instruction: Score 10 when computational cost, memory, latency, data requirements, or deployment constraints are quantified alongside the claimed capability; score 0 when efficiency or practicality is asserted without resource accounting.
selected.rationale: R29 makes encryption-related fine-tuning and inference costs central and quantifies both. R14 connects hardware utilization, sequence length, training speed, and generation speed to its architectural choices.

selected.name: Abstract Length Brevity
selected.instruction: Score from 0 (very long) to 10 (very short) based strictly on the word count of the abstract text. Do not judge the quality of the length, only measure how brief it is.
selected.rationale: Length can arbitrarily bias a scorecard model that rewards completeness, while a dense model might penalize excessively short abstracts that fail to fully explain the methodology (e.g., the very brief R15 versus the more standard length of R02).
member_names: Abstract bulk: length plus enumerated contribution expansiveness

selected.name: Density of numeric performance claims and superlative comparisons
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the abstract packs explicit quantitative result claims and comparative superlatives into its text. Count: numerals attached to results (percentages, accuracy or AP or PPL values, 'x' speedup factors, counts of benchmarks or datasets beaten) and comparison phrases such as 'outperforms state-of-the-art', 'significantly outperforms', 'by a large margin', 'achieves the best'. 0 = no result numerals and no comparative superlatives; 5 = one or two numeric results, or one superlative claim; 10 = many numeric deltas plus repeated superlative comparison language. You must NOT verify, weigh, or judge whether the numbers are impressive, correct, or well earned, and must NOT treat their absence as a flaw; report only how much of this reporting style is present.
selected.rationale: Numeric-superiority packaging concentrates in the card-high half of the slice: R10 (92.7 percent versus 28.5 percent, plus 49.5 percent black-box), R29 (43.9 AP, 4.1 higher than baseline), R41 (116.4 percent, 23.2 percent, 23.7 percent, 11 of 18 datasets) and R56 (6.94x and 2.3x). The dense-high half often has nothing numeric to state: R39, R08, R26 and R54 report qualitatively, and R44 and R22 are theory papers where a percentage would be meaningless. The channel therefore tracks which genre the paper belongs to and how its community writes results, not whether the work is sound; a theory paper cannot earn the tick and an incremental benchmark paper earns it automatically.
member_names: Density of numeric performance claims and superlative comparisons
selected.upstream_parent: subfield and genre reporting convention (empirical-benchmark paper versus theory or analysis paper)
upstream_parent_all_members: subfield and genre reporting convention (empirical-benchmark paper versus theory or analysis paper)

selected.name: Signalled scale of compute, data, and evaluation breadth
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract advertises the SIZE of the resources behind it: parameter counts, corpus or dataset sizes, number of models or baselines evaluated, number of benchmarks or environments used, quantity of human annotation collected, scale of training runs. 0 = no scale of any kind stated; 5 = one dataset or benchmark named at modest scale; 10 = several explicit large magnitudes, for example hundreds of millions of items, dozens of models compared, or many benchmark suites at once. You must NOT judge whether the scale is appropriate, necessary, sufficient, or impressive, and must NOT treat small scale as a weakness; count only how much scale is stated in the text.
selected.rationale: Advertised scale is a direct textual fingerprint of budget, which is very unevenly distributed across submitters. R27 states 18K curated questions across 26 subcategories and 22 open-source plus 6 closed-source models evaluated; R25 states a memory of 150 million Wikipedia mentions; R60 states 6,790 annotated events with human labellers; R37 reports scaling to 2.7B parameters on the Pile; R13 reports a Mechanical Turk human evaluation and a google-research release path. A criterion bank containing items about thorough evaluation or dataset ambition will fire on budget rather than on insight, and R08, R50 and R54 can never earn those ticks. Tagged mixed because budget does buy some genuine thoroughness.
member_names: Signalled scale of compute, data, and evaluation breadth

selected.name: Trendy Topic Jargon Density
selected.instruction: 0-10, to what extent does the abstract feature a high density of highly popular, trendy terms (e.g., 'LLMs', 'GPT-4', 'NeRF', 'CLIP')? 0 means none; 10 means the abstract is overwhelmingly packed with trendy jargon. Do not judge the actual quality of the research.
selected.rationale: Authors often explicitly anchor their work to highly popular, trendy models or concepts to ride the wave of current research attention. R04 repeatedly mentions models like Llama-2 and OpenLLaMA, while R45 leans heavily on 'LLM Agents'. This acts as a temporal tell and audience hook that is predictive of visibility but not inherently tied to the underlying research quality.

selected.name: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of explicit release and availability announcements in the abstract: a code URL, a GitHub or project-page or website link, phrases such as 'code is available', 'our data and code will be available', 'code has been released', or the naming of released checkpoints, benchmarks, annotations or datasets as deliverables. 0 = no availability statement of any kind; 3 = a bare promise of future release with no link; 6 = one concrete link or one clearly named released artifact; 10 = several artifacts announced together (for example code plus data plus model weights plus a project page). You must NOT assess whether releasing is good practice, whether the link looks credible or maintained, or whether the artifact is valuable; count only how prominently availability is announced.
selected.rationale: Availability sentences cluster in the card-high half of this slice: R01, R05, R10, R33, R43, R45, R48 and R56 all close with a link or an explicit promise, while several dense-high entries make no such announcement at all (R54, R44, R14, R15, R34, R57). A judge working from a fixed criterion bank can tick a reproducibility or openness item off that one sentence without any of the underlying artifact being visible, and the sentence is produced by group practice, engineering capacity and institutional permission rather than by the research itself. Tagged mixed because the same practice plausibly co-occurs with genuinely more careful and checkable work.
member_names: Artifact-availability boilerplate: code, data, project-page announcements

selected.name: Problem-solution template cadence
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, judge how strongly the abstract follows a stock sequence of problem, limitations, proposed method, and experimental confirmation; assess rhetorical structure only, never whether the argument or method is good.
selected.rationale: Template familiarity can make prose easier to parse without establishing scientific merit. The cadence is visible in R06, R24, R25, and R49.

selected.name: Artifact-release signaling
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, judge how much the abstract advertises code, data, models, checkpoints, or project pages; assess only the extent of release signaling, never whether the artifacts are useful or reproducible.
selected.rationale: Artifact signaling can shape reader expectations independently of the underlying contribution, while the same practice may also accompany genuine engineering quality. It appears in R05, R15, R27, and R54.

selected.name: Names a live unsolved difficulty and its specific departure
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text. Score 0-10 how precisely the abstract (a) identifies a specific technical difficulty or failure mode that current approaches do not handle, and (b) states concretely what this work does differently in response to that difficulty - a named mechanism, assumption dropped, constraint relaxed, resource removed, or setting extended. Judge the substance in context. You are explicitly instructed NOT to reward fashionable vocabulary, named paradigms, or the apparent popularity of the topic: a term-dense abstract earns nothing here unless the difficulty and the departure are actually stated. 10 = the abstract pins down the exact obstacle (what breaks, under what conditions, for which prior approach) and the exact change made, in enough detail that a reader could restate both in one sentence; this must be reachable by a short, plainly written abstract on an unfashionable subject with no trendy terms at all. 0 = the abstract gestures at an area, a paradigm or a general 'challenge' without ever naming a concrete obstacle or a concrete departure, however current-sounding the vocabulary.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause, submission timing and community fashion, can produce genuine merit in one way: work aimed at a currently active frontier may be engaging a difficulty that is genuinely open, and that merit shows up as a nameable obstacle plus a nameable change - never as terminology. This criterion asks only for that nameable pair, in context, and forbids credit for the vocabulary carrier. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: an abstract on numerical conditioning of an old estimator, written in ordinary words with zero fashionable terms, which states that existing solvers diverge when the design matrix is rank-deficient and that this work replaces the inversion step with a projection - scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: an abstract that stacks LLM, diffusion, foundation-model and agentic language across every sentence but only says it explores the potential of these paradigms for a domain - scores near 10 on the surface component and 0 here.
member_names: Names a live unsolved difficulty and its specific departure

selected.name: Density of currently fashionable technical terms and paradigm names
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text and count. Score 0-10 the extent to which currently fashionable technical terms and named paradigms occur - for example large language model or LLM, diffusion, NeRF, Transformer, foundation model, agentic, in-context, multimodal, scaling law, and comparable buzz-carrying labels of the moment. Estimate both how many distinct such terms appear and how often they recur, and combine into one extent score. 0 = no such terms anywhere. 3 = one such term appearing once or twice. 6 = two or three distinct such terms recurring through the abstract. 10 = four or more distinct fashionable terms, several of them repeated, saturating most sentences. You are explicitly instructed NOT to decide whether using these terms is good, bad, appropriate, or earned, and NOT to consider whether the work behind them is sound; score only how much of this vocabulary is present.
selected.rationale: This is the pure fingerprint of the conjectured upstream cause - it registers the vocabulary a fashionable submission window deposits on the page, with every trace of merit stripped out, and is answerable by counting alone. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: a term-saturated abstract that promises to investigate foundation-model agents for a domain, with no obstacle and no mechanism stated, scores 10 here and 0 on the candidate-real component. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: the rank-deficiency abstract above, which names its obstacle and its exact fix in plain unfashionable words, scores 0 here and near 10 on the candidate-real component.
member_names: Density of currently fashionable technical terms and paradigm names
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Trend-term concentration

selected.name: Claims specified precisely enough to be checked by a reader
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text. Score 0-10 how precisely the abstract pins down what was actually accomplished, so that a reader could in principle go and check it: the specific task or system acted on, the conditions or setting it was measured under, the comparison point it is being contrasted with, and what quantity was measured. Judge specification, in context - NOT how exciting, memorable, picturable or plainly worded the accomplishment is, and NOT how large it sounds. A dry numeric result is fully eligible for 10 if its task, setting, baseline and measured quantity are all stated. 10 = every claimed accomplishment is tied to a named task or system, a stated setting or condition, and an explicit comparison point, so nothing essential is left for the reader to guess. 0 = the accomplishments are asserted in unanchored terms (better, state of the art, strong performance, solves the problem, first of its kind) with no task, condition, comparison or measured quantity attached.
selected.rationale: The merit that a genuinely completed endpoint produces is checkability: a group that really reached a milestone can say exactly what, where, against what, and measured how. That substance is separable from the plain-language vividness that carries it. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: an abstract reporting only percentage deltas but stating the exact dataset, the held-out split, the specific baseline method and the metric - scores near 10 here while scoring 0 on the surface component because it names no picturable milestone. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: an abstract announcing that the system is the first ever to beat a human champion at a named board game, with no setting, no conditions, no opponent pool and no measured quantity - scores 10 on the surface component and near 0 here.
selected.parent: Concrete, vivid endpoint achievement stated in plain language
member_names: Claims specified precisely enough to be checked by a reader

selected.name: Amount of vivid, picturable, plain-language milestone phrasing
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text and estimate extent. Score 0-10 how much of the abstract's achievement language is vivid, everyday and easily pictured rather than abstract or numeric: named games, physical objects, robots, real-world tasks or artefacts a non-specialist could visualise; superlative milestone framings such as first to, human-level, beats a professional, solves; concrete scene-setting nouns. Count how many such phrasings appear and how prominently they are placed. 0 = achievements appear only as abstract numbers, deltas or technical quantities, with nothing picturable. 5 = one picturable or milestone phrase somewhere in the abstract. 10 = several vivid, easily visualised milestone phrasings, including at least one in the opening or closing sentence. You are explicitly instructed NOT to judge whether the vivid claim is true, important, verifiable, or well supported, and NOT to reward or penalise the underlying work; score only how much vivid plain-language milestone phrasing is on the page.
selected.rationale: Memorability of phrasing is the carrier: it is a property of how the endpoint is worded, countable without any assessment of whether the endpoint is real or specified. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: the unanchored first-to-beat-a-champion abstract above scores 10 here and near 0 on the candidate-real component. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: the fully specified dataset-split-baseline-metric abstract scores 0 here, since nothing in it is picturable, and near 10 on the candidate-real component.
selected.parent: Concrete, vivid endpoint achievement stated in plain language
member_names: Amount of vivid, picturable, plain-language milestone phrasing
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Concrete, vivid endpoint achievement stated in plain language

selected.name: Share of the text carrying specific technical content
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text. Score 0-10 the proportion of the writing that carries specific, checkable technical content - the problem setting, the mechanism of the method, what was set up or measured, the conditions, the scope or limits - as opposed to framing, motivation, importance claims, restatement and generic transitions. This is a density judgement, normalised by the words spent: you are explicitly instructed that longer is NOT higher and shorter is NOT lower, and that a long abstract stacking many low-content sentences must score low. 10 = nearly every clause adds a new specific about the problem, the mechanism, the setup or the scope, with essentially no filler; a three-sentence abstract can and should reach 10 if those three sentences do this. 0 = the text is almost entirely importance framing, restated motivation and generic claims, with the actual method and setup left unspecified, at any length.
selected.rationale: The merit that lies behind textual volume is the amount actually said: an author with a fully worked-out contribution has more specifics to fit in. Isolating the share of substance rather than the quantity of text lets a terse abstract win and blocks the length carrier from reaching the top end. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: a two-sentence abstract that states the setting, the exact estimator change, the evaluation setup and the scope limit scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: a 300-word abstract of importance framing, field background and repeated promises that never states a mechanism or a setup scores 10 on the surface component and near 0 here.
member_names: Share of the text carrying specific technical content

selected.name: Raw textual volume in words and sentences
selected.instruction: Read only the abstract text and measure volume. Score 0-10 the raw amount of text present, by estimating the number of words and the number of sentences. 0 = extremely terse, roughly 1-3 sentences or under about 40 words. 3 = about 60-90 words. 5 = about 100-140 words. 7 = about 160-200 words. 10 = about 250 words or more, or many sentences across multiple paragraph-length stretches. Interpolate between these anchors. You are explicitly instructed NOT to judge whether the length is appropriate, whether the text is padded or efficient, or whether the underlying work is good; score only the extent of textual volume on the page.
selected.rationale: Word count is the pure carrier of the parent channel: countable, and completely indifferent to whether anything is said. Dissociation high-surface / low-real: the 300-word all-framing abstract scores 10 here and near 0 on the candidate-real component. Dissociation high-real / low-surface: the dense two-sentence abstract scores near 0 here and near 10 on the candidate-real component.
member_names: Raw textual volume in words and sentences
